title: Dr. Kassaye's Sample Review Questions
description: The 15 sample review questions Dr. Kassaye posted for the Fall 2026 midterm. No key was given; 14 are word-for-word publisher test-bank items, so their keys and explanations come from the vetted bank.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 1 · Q17).

questions.prompt: Robert Rennie, the Chief Operating Officer of Clearwater Industrial Products, is interviewed by TV reporters about recent allegations that the company has been dumping toxic waste into a stream. According to Mintzberg, Robert is performing the managerial role of
questions.explanation: Speaking to the press for the organization is the **spokesperson role**, which sends messages into the external environment. A disseminator passes information to people inside the organization.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 3 · Q9).

questions.prompt: The chairperson opened the meeting by saying “I’m sure you all agree with me that….”. What perceptual phenomenon might the speaker be exhibiting:
questions.explanation: **Projection** is assuming others feel as you do, as when the chairperson assumes everyone agrees. It is not stereotyping, because no social category is involved.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 3 · Q45).

questions.prompt: A manager of an employment agency uses a trick question to get companies to hire his candidates. If the agency only has a marginal candidate for a specific position, the manager sends over two obviously unqualified/incompetent candidates to be interviewed before sending over the “acceptable” person. Which perceptual mechanism is the agency manager relying on to get the marginal candidate hired?
questions.explanation: Sending two real duds first exploits the **contrast effect**: previous applicants exaggerate the difference to the current one, so the marginal candidate looks better. The halo effect concerns one trait colouring others.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 2 · Q10).

questions.prompt: Gary Reynolds is the CEO of Reynolds Software Ltd. He attributes his success to careful planning, hard work, and a good business education. In terms of locus of control, Gary is most likely a(n)
questions.explanation: Gary credits his own planning and effort for his success, which marks an **internal locus of control**. Externals credit luck, fate, or powerful people. Extraversion and self-monitoring are different dimensions.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 2 · Q52).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is related to the probability of obtaining employment?
questions.explanation: High **conscientiousness** in adolescence is related to lower unemployment throughout adulthood, so it is linked to the probability of being employed. Other traits are tied to income or satisfaction instead.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 4 · Q14).

questions.prompt: A fairly stable evaluative tendency to respond consistently to some specific object, situation, person, or category of people is called a(n)
questions.explanation: An **attitude** is a fairly stable evaluative tendency to respond consistently to a specific object, situation, person or group. A value is broader and about general preferences.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 4 · Q4).

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the cultural value of power is false?

options.text: In high power distance cultures the unequal distribution of power is acceptable to members of a culture
Japan has higher power distance than Canada
Denmark has lower power distance than Mexico
Superiors tend to be accessible in low power distance cultures
High power distance cultures tend to also be individualistic, rather than collective cultures

questions.explanation: High power distance cultures tend to be **collectivistic**, not individualistic; individualistic cultures downplay power differences. The other statements match the text, including Japan being higher than Canada.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 5 · Q6).

questions.prompt: “An interesting job that pays well” suggests that the job:

options.text: Is high in intrinsic but low in extrinsic motivation
Is low in intrinsic and high in extrinsic motivation
Is high in intrinsic and extrinsic motivation

questions.explanation: Interesting work is an **intrinsic** motivator and good pay is an **extrinsic** one, so the job has both. The text notes that some motivators even have both qualities at once.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 5 · Q22).

questions.prompt: McClelland’s need for affiliation is most closely related to Alderfer’s ______________ need.
questions.explanation: McClelland's **need for affiliation** is a belongingness or **relatedness** need, since it is about establishing and maintaining friendly relationships. Growth better matches nAch, and existence is material needs.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 5 · Q29).

questions.prompt: According to the expectancy theory of motivation, if we find that workers feel that they are unable to perform at a high level, we are dealing with a problem of:
questions.explanation: Feeling unable to perform at a high level is a problem of **expectancy**, the probability that effort will achieve a first-level outcome. Instrumentality concerns whether performance is rewarded.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 5 · Q53).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a good practical example of goal challenge?

options.text: To encourage a D student to set a goal of achieving Cs in the coming semester
To encourage a D student to set a goal of achieving Bs in the coming semester
To encourage a D student to set a goal of achieving As in the coming semester
To encourage a D student to set a goal of achieving Ds in the coming semester
To set no goal as goals are not motivating

questions.explanation: Goal challenge should be pegged to ability, using **past performance** as the base: a D student aims for Cs. Another D is too easy, and Bs or As may be seen as impossible, so they lose motivating power.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 10 · Q13).

questions.prompt: Sticking with the strict chain of command is most likely to impede ___________ communication.
questions.explanation: Under a strict chain of command, a **horizontal** message has to go up to a common manager and back down, which makes it slow. Upward and downward messages follow the chain naturally.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 10 · Q47).

questions.prompt: The performance appraisal system that has been adopted by several companies to enhance communication is called:
questions.explanation: Using superiors, self, subordinates, peers and clients as raters is **multisource or 360-degree feedback**. Calling it 180-degree feedback or peer review misses most of the sources.

source.note: Also in the publisher test bank (Ch 11 · Q14).

questions.prompt: In evaluating alternative solutions, decision-makers with bounded rationality

options.text: Know the ultimate value of each alternative
Know the probability that each alternative will work
Often consider the political acceptability of the solution to other organizational members

questions.explanation: Under **bounded rationality** decision makers weigh extra criteria such as political acceptability (will the boss like it?). Knowing every alternative's value and probability, and maximizing, describe perfect rationality; bounded decision makers usually **satisfice**.

questions.prompt: Individual decision-making can be impacted by use of a judgmental heuristic. Which of the following best defines a heuristic?

options.text: A judgement shortcut or rule of thumb

questions.explanation: A **heuristic** is a judgment shortcut or rule of thumb that saves effort when deciding. The lecture's **availability** and **representativeness** biases are heuristics that can mislead. Hindsight is a separate bias, and the cue options are made-up distractors.
